TEN-1.title: Tenant comes from the credential only
TEN-1.mechanism: `TenantScopeMiddleware` reads `tenant_id` from the JWT only; `EndpointSpineTests` scans route and query parameters enumerated BY EXCLUSION and DECLARED tenant/PII headers via the framework's own `IFromHeaderMetadata` with vendor-prefix and separator normalization, matching both with `NameComparison`; `HostSecurityTests` proves at run time that a forged tenant header in five spellings does not move a request into another tenant; `ContractShapeTests` bans `TenantId` on requests
TEN-1.note: TEN-1 names four surfaces and this edition reaches all four, unevenly. ROUTE is total, because the pattern loop reads parameter names without consulting a type. HEADER is covered from both sides (A-2): a declared binding is a scan violation, and a header arriving undeclared is proven not to influence tenant resolution. QUERY was type-dependent and is not any more (E-2, repaired 2026-07-27): nothing asks what binds from a URL, so a strong-typed tenant id is inside the surface by default, proven by planting `TenantKeyProbe : IParsable` as a query parameter named `tenantKey` on a real route (red now, green under the old mechanism). Matching was equality and is now a comparison (E-9, repaired), which matters most on the header surface, where normalization removes every boundary a token matcher would need. **The row is still `owed` on one surface only: the request contract**, because that half rests on `ContractShapeTests`, which is flat, and repairing it means opening MOD-2's realization before MOD-2 has had its delta pass. Findings: A-2 (repaired), E-2 (repaired), E-9 (repaired), E-6 (contracts half open). Request-contract surface raised 2026-07-27, together with E-22's repair of the tenant predicate on body members.

obligations.name: the tenant is resolved solely from the validated credential
obligations.text: `TenantScopeMiddleware` reads `tenant_id` from the token and from nothing else, which is the half of this claim the second edition cannot reach at all because it can mint no credential.

obligations.name: the route surface is enumerated completely
obligations.text: the pattern loop reads parameter names without consulting a type, so no route parameter is invisible to it; what the predicate then does with the name is the comparison obligation below.

obligations.name: the query surface is enumerated completely
obligations.text: the hand-written type list is gone: parameters are enumerated by exclusion from the composed route table, so a value object implementing the framework's parse interface, a `TimeSpan` or a type nobody has thought of is inside the surface rather than outside it, and the enumeration is held to agree with the real binder over E-2's measured corpus rather than restating the binder's rules in an assertion (E-2).

obligations.name: the header surface has a mechanism of its own
obligations.text: a header surface cannot be enumerated, so this is the non-scan mechanism ruling 5 requires, and it is covered from both sides: a DECLARED header binding is a scan violation through the framework's own `IFromHeaderMetadata`, with vendor-prefix and separator normalization, and a header arriving UNDECLARED is proven at run time not to move a request into another tenant, in five spellings (A-2). The normalization compacts `X-Tenant-Id` to `tenantid`, which destroys every boundary; the comparison resolves the concatenation, so the base entry covers it without a list of pre-glued spellings (E-9).

obligations.name: the request-contract surface is enumerated completely
obligations.text: repaired 2026-07-27, and raising it exposed a gap no pass had named. The contracts guard now walks every member at any depth through the shared `BodyMemberWalk`, which closes the enumeration half. The predicate half was missing outright: the tenant registry was applied to URL parameters and to nothing else, so a request contract carrying `WorkspaceId` and `OrganisationId` passed all 100 tests while TEN-1's statement says no request contract carries a tenant identifier field. Only `tenantId` was caught, and only because SEC-2's separate registry happens to list it. Both surfaces now apply the tenant registry to body members, proven red on an unrouted contract and on the routed `CreateNoteRequest`, green when reverted. Recorded as E-22.

obligations.name: the comparison resolves compounds, concatenations and decompositions of a listed word
obligations.text: matching is `NameComparison`: an entry `tenant` covers `tenantId`, `tenantid`, `tenant_id` and `tenantSlug`, an entry `org` covers `orgId` and `orgid` through a declared affix, and the flow-back pass's widened list of compounds is gone because they are derived, each asserted to still match. The prefix rule that would let `org` reach `organisationid` directly is rejected and asserted against, because it also matches `origin`, an ordinary request header (E-9).

SEC-1.title: Every endpoint gated
SEC-1.mechanism: deny-by-default fallback policy (a deny, not `RequireAuthenticatedUser`, so a metadata-free endpoint is unreachable rather than open to every authenticated caller) + cached `PermissionPolicyProvider`; `EndpointSpineTests` resolves the fallback from `IAuthorizationPolicyProvider`, which is what the middleware consults, and EVALUATES it against an anonymous principal and a fully-permissioned authenticated one; it also allowlists `/health` and requires a permission policy per endpoint; the `sv`/tenant gates run after routing and exempt allowlisted-anonymous endpoints
SEC-1.note: The anonymous allowlist is a `(Method, Pattern, Why)` record array as of 2026-07-26 (E-8): keyed on method AND pattern so an anonymous GET no longer pre-authorizes a POST on the same URL, carrying a mandatory justification, matched case-insensitively, and failing on an entry that matches no endpoint. All four proven red separately. The fallback applies to unmatched URLs too, so an unknown route answers 403 rather than 404. The HUM-1 half of E-8 stays open: there is nowhere to declare this surface such that the shared tool VERIFIES an owner exists, which is an adjudication ruling. Findings: E-7 (repaired), E-8 (SEC-1 half repaired, HUM-1 half open).

SEC-2.title: Anti mass-assignment
SEC-2.mechanism: `EndpointSpineTests` takes each endpoint's body type from the framework's own `IAcceptsMetadata` and walks it RECURSIVELY through public properties, constructor parameters, arrays and generic arguments, with cycle protection and no depth cap, matched by `NameComparison` against the shared registry, with a parameter walk as a second net and a non-vacuity assertion; `ContractShapeTests` is a third net over the Contracts assembly, FLAT and filtered to types whose name ends in `Request`, matching by equality; App/Api declare no request/response types
SEC-2.note: The guards are not equivalent and the difference is the point. The HOST scan recurses (E-6, 2026-07-26) and as of 2026-07-27 it no longer decides for itself what a body is: the enumeration comes from the framework's `IAcceptsMetadata`, so the two exclusions that used to hide a type from it are gone. Both were proven by planting the violation on a real route: a public DTO declared in the entry-point file, which has no namespace and was skipped outright, is now caught, and the old mechanism with the same DTO planted is green. The comparison is no longer equality (E-9). **`ContractShapeTests` is STILL FLAT and still enumerates only `*Request` types**, and that is why the row is still `owed`: repairing it means opening MOD-2's realization before MOD-2 has had its delta pass, which is a decision for the owner and not for this pass. The residual it leaves was measured rather than argued: a `*Request` contract carrying a forbidden field one level down, bound to no route, is invisible to both guards; the moment it is bound to a route the host scan catches it at depth. So the uncovered set is exactly the contract types nothing can post to. Findings: E-2 (repaired), E-6 (host half repaired, contracts half blocked on MOD-2), E-9 (repaired), E-20. Enumeration raised 2026-07-27: the contracts guard now shares the endpoint scan's walk and comparison, and the tenant registry reaches contract members for the first time (E-22).

obligations.name: the predicate rejects a registry member at any depth of an enumerated type
obligations.text: `EndpointSpineTests` walks every body-bound DTO recursively through public properties, constructor parameters, arrays and generic arguments, with cycle protection and no depth cap, proven both ways against a nested `AuthorDto` carrying `CreatedBy` (E-6), and the walk's depth is asserted directly because the composed host binds only flat records today.

obligations.name: the enumeration reaches every body-bound type
obligations.text: both nets are now complete and they share one walk. The host half takes the body type from the framework's own `IAcceptsMetadata.RequestType` rather than from a predicate of this test's own, so E-6's null-namespace exclusion and E-2's hand-written type list are both gone. The second net, `ContractShapeTests`, was the last flat and equality-matching guard in the tree and is repaired: it walks the SAME `BodyMemberWalk.MemberNames` at any depth and compares through the SAME `NameComparison`, so the two guards cannot drift apart about what a caller can populate. Proven with a control: with the pre-repair guard restored and an unrouted `OrphanRequest` carrying `AuthorInfo.CreatedBy` planted, all 100 tests passed; with the repair, the nested field and a `CreatedByUser` compound at depth zero each fail separately. The residual, stated: a contract type in the Contracts assembly that is neither routed nor named `*Request` is enumerated by neither guard, and nothing can post to it, so it enters the surface only by gaining a route, at which point the host scan sees it. It was repaired here after three passes recorded it as blocked on MOD-2's delta; that premise was measured and is false (S-12).

obligations.name: the comparison resolves compounds, concatenations and decompositions of a listed word
obligations.text: matching is `NameComparison`, not a hash-set lookup: `status` covers `noteStatus` and `notestatus`, `createdAt` covers `createdAtUtc`, `role` covers `roles`, and the registry lost the spellings it used to enumerate because they are derived, each one asserted to still match. The flat second net still compares by equality and reads the same registry, and a test holds every name in the flat list to be matched by the rules, so the weaker net can never become a different one (E-9).

SEC-3.title: No PII in URLs
SEC-3.mechanism: `EndpointSpineTests` route + query scan over the composed route table, enumerated BY EXCLUSION (the framework's own declared body type, registered services and the pipeline's own types are set aside and every other parameter is a value a caller can spell), with [AsParameters] wrapper properties walked; matched by `NameComparison`, which resolves compounds, concatenations, decompositions and plurals
SEC-3.note: Lowered from `proven` to `owed` by the adjudication pass of 2026-07-26 (ruling 6), and **both named gaps were closed on 2026-07-27**: the enumeration no longer asks which types bind from a URL (E-2) and the comparison is no longer equality (E-9). Each was proven by planting the violation on a real route in the composed host, confirming red, then restoring the old mechanism with the violation still planted and confirming green, which reproduces the hole rather than taking the record's word for it. The row does not return to `proven`, and the reason is a duty the row never carried: SEC-3's completeness obligation ends "a query parameter the surface does not declare is refused or removed before the handler by a ruled decision, never bound silently", and nothing here does that. Measured, not inferred: a handler that takes HttpContext and reads `Request.Query["emailAddress"]` leaves the scan green. That obligation is written into the row below rather than left in prose, so the row reads `owed` for something real (E-20).

obligations.name: the predicate rejects a registry match on a parameter it can see
obligations.text: `EndpointSpineTests` scans route and query parameters, covering `[AsParameters]` wrappers, collections and date parameter types that a naive scan misses.

obligations.name: the enumeration reaches every declared route and query parameter
obligations.text: the hand-written type list is gone. Nothing asks what binds from a URL any more: the body type comes from the framework's own `IAcceptsMetadata` on the composed endpoint, services come from `IServiceProviderIsService`, the pipeline's own types are a closed list of things no caller can spell a value for, and every other parameter is compared. A type nobody has thought of is inside the surface by default instead of outside it. `Both_enumerations_agree_with_the_real_binder_over_a_corpus_of_parameter_types` holds that against the binder that actually runs, over E-2's measured corpus (`TenantKey : IParsable`, `TimeSpan`, `Uri`, `IPAddress`, `Int128`, a legacy `TryParse` type), so the two can no longer drift apart silently (E-2).

obligations.name: the comparison resolves compounds, concatenations, decompositions and plurals of a listed word
obligations.text: `NameComparison` tokenizes on camel case, separators and letter/digit boundaries, re-glues every contiguous run of tokens, matches an entry that begins or ends a glued word, folds plurals, and derives an entry's tail past a one-letter particle, so `email` covers `emailAddress`, `user_email`, `emailaddress`, `e_mail`, `e-mail`, `EMailAddress`, `mail`, `emails` and `email1`. It beats both matchers this repo has built: the six inputs the round 4 audit measured escaping BOTH equality and token matching are asserted, and the registry got SHORTER because `firstname`, `lastname` and `dateofbirth` are derived rather than listed, with every dropped spelling asserted to still match. Its false positives (`fileName`, `voicemail`) and its residuals (a synonym, a reordering, an unnamed parameter) are passing tests, so a later narrowing goes red (E-9).

obligations.name: a parameter that binds or is read without being declared is inside the surface
obligations.text: SEC-3's remedy sentence requires an undeclared query parameter to be "refused or removed before the handler by a ruled decision, never bound silently", and this edition has no such mechanism: measured, a handler taking HttpContext and reading `Request.Query["emailAddress"]` leaves the whole suite green. TEN-1 met the same shape on the header surface with a runtime mechanism rather than a scan, which is the available answer here, and refuse-versus-remove is exactly the choice the claim says must be RULED per surface (trigger: an adjudication ruling on the refuse-or-remove decision, in the class of E-8's HUM-1 half; the row is `owed` on this and on nothing else).

SEC-5.title: No secrets in config
SEC-5.mechanism: `UserSecretsId` + `SecretConfigShapeTests` over every committed JSON config under `src/`, matching secret-shaped keys by TOKEN (camel/Pascal/snake/kebab split) rather than by containment, with a `[Theory]` asserting the predicate's extent + `tools/secret-scan.mjs`, a composed shared-tier scan over every tracked text surface with a `--self-test` mode CI runs before the scan
SEC-5.note: Both mechanisms were blind to the edition's own `Jwt:Key` until 2026-07-26 and both are repaired (E-11). The arch test matched `leafKey.Contains(term)`, which could never fire on a leaf shorter than the term describing it; the CI half was a grep in YAML that was additionally blind to every QUOTED key, meaning every key in every JSON file in the edition (E-16). Four justified exceptions are declared in `secret-scan.allow.json`, each a (file, key) pair with a written reason and a staleness check; one of them is a committed test signing key the repaired scan found on its first run (E-17). Token matching costs a false positive on `TokenCount`, asserted as a passing case rather than hidden (E-9). Still open: `.env` lives inside the repository tree while the claim's statement says development secrets live outside it (E-12), which the scan's tracked-file reading does NOT address. Vault-port interface owed (trigger: first runtime credential).

obligations.name: no secret-shaped value in committed configuration
obligations.text: `SecretConfigShapeTests` over every committed JSON config under `src/`, matching secret-shaped keys by token split rather than by containment, with a `[Theory]` asserting the predicate's extent.

TIME-1.title: UTC, offset-aware, and nothing else
TIME-1.mechanism: `TimeTypeTests` over every layer project under server/src, DERIVED from the filesystem rather than listed (recurses Nullable, arrays, generics; the global namespace is app code, not framework); a layer that exists and whose assembly the scan cannot reach fails a test of its own
TIME-1.note: DB UTC column defaults not used: the service sets the value. **Lowered from `proven` to `owed` by the adjudication pass of 2026-07-26 (rulings 2 and 3).** E-15 measured the omitted layer with a control and the flow-back pass deliberately did not repair it, on the grounds that lowering the row belonged to the owner. **The layer half was repaired on 2026-07-27**, and not by adding the missing assembly to the list: the list is gone and the layer set is derived from the projects under server/src, which is what TIME-1 requires ("a rule the test can check rather than a hand-written list"). Proven three ways, each red before the repair and after the violation was planted: a naive `DateTime` on a public type in the API layer, the same type declared in the entry-point file where it has no namespace at all (the file E-6 and E-15 both exempt), and a layer added under src/ that the tests cannot reach, which fails without carrying any time type. The monotonic-durations half has never had a realization here and is why the row still reads `owed`, which is the S-11 shape: two obligations that are built, gating and red-green proven, rolled up with one deferred extension, and the vocabulary's weakest word means "not built".

obligations.name: the predicate rejects a naive instant in the layers it reaches
obligations.text: `TimeTypeTests` recurses Nullable, arrays and generics over the layers it is given, and rejects naive `DateTime` in all of them. As of 2026-07-27 it also walks types with no namespace, which the hierarchy walk previously stopped at as though the global namespace were the framework.

obligations.name: the enumeration reaches every layer that declares a time value
obligations.text: the layer set is derived from the projects under server/src, so a layer added to the server is scanned with no edit to the test, and a layer that exists and whose assembly the scan cannot reach fails `Every_declared_layer_is_reachable_by_the_scan` rather than being skipped, which is the remedy half TIME-1 asks for ("a layer that exists and is not in the enumeration fails the build too"). The derivation is cross-checked against the composed host's own assembly graph so an empty walk cannot read green. E-15's control is red both ways now, and so is the one that composes with E-6 on the entry-point file.

UI-1.title: Token source lockstep
UI-1.mechanism: `tokenCoverage.test.ts` reads the export at its canonical home `design/prototype/_ds/colors_and_type.css` (every CSS var has a token, count > 50)
UI-1.note: Lowered from `proven` to `latent` on 2026-07-27 by the acceptance test. The mechanism binds and is not in question; its SUBJECT is the kernel`s own placeholder. `design/prototype/_ds/colors_and_type.css` ships 58 variables, deliberately over the floor of 50, and its own header says to replace it with a real export at instantiation, so `tokenCoverage.test.ts` goes green in a seeded project whose design system is the kernel`s filler and whose product design does not exist. That is `latent` by the vocabulary`s own definition: the mechanism exists and has had no real subject yet. Compounding it, manifest step 6 demands the complete design export at seed time, which the method`s own skill order makes impossible (seed runs immediately after gate 1; the export is two skills away, behind decompose and design), and it duplicates x2:lock. The manifest offers no fallback and part C admits no blocked state (E-27). TEST-3 and HUM-1 both carry an instantiation asterisk; this row needed one and did not have it. Finding: E-27.

UI-2.title: Literal visual values are lint errors
UI-2.mechanism: `eslint.config.js` bans visual literals in styles: colors, font props, radii, hairlines, and spacing/dimension literals (numerics matched on `raw`), with the structural allowlist
UI-2.note: the ban is not total: bare negative numerics escape every dimension selector, because the numeric selectors use a direct-child combinator and a negative parses as Property > UnaryExpression > Literal, and the per-side axes (borderTopWidth, outline) are in no alternation (E-31). Planted 2026-07-27, nine plants, seven red naming UI-2. The config itself is fixture-free and can be narrowed to reach nothing with `npm run verify` green (E-30).

obligations.name: error-tier rules ban literal visual values and gate the client verification chain
obligations.text: planted 2026-07-27 across seven categories (hex, named colour, bare dimension, px string, radius, border shorthand, fontWeight); each failed `eslint .` with the message naming UI-2, and `verify` short-circuits on it.

obligations.name: coverage of every axis and every syntactic form a literal can take
obligations.text: `marginTop: -8` and `borderTopWidth: 1` both pass (E-31). Each newly gated axis and each newly reachable syntactic form owes its own selector, which is the standing debt this tag names.

DEP-1.title: Dependency quarantine
DEP-1.mechanism: CPM exact pins + lockfiles + locked-mode restore (`--locked-mode` / `npm ci`) + `VERSIONS.md` (30-day window header, container-images section, kernel-provenance section) + docs-lint ledger, image, and kernel-provenance checks; the SQL Server image is one tag@digest value across runbook, CI, and the Testcontainers fixture
DEP-1.note: publish-date CI check owed (dates recorded by hand); kernel-provenance check latent until the next instantiation fills a real pin; the CI toolchain itself is unpinned and carries no ledger rows (E-1, not repaired). The shared client tier was re-planned against the 30-day window on 2026-07-26 (E-3): 14 advisories to 1 root, 0 critical, verified by `npm ci` and `npm run verify` in both editions. `postcss` GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 had no release satisfying both the window and the advisory, and DEP-1 gained the resolution order at adjudication ruling 9a on 2026-07-26: the advisory outranks the window above the 7-day floor, by explicit decision, with a ledger row for the pin whether it is direct or transitive. The override moved to 8.5.18 in the shared tier and `npm audit` over that tier now reports 0 vulnerabilities, down from 1 high. The pin is the first row of VERSIONS.md's advisory-rule section and leaves it on 2026-08-11 (E-18). Planted 2026-07-27, seventeen plants: four red-correct, twelve green, one red-different. The lockfile-drift remedy fails the build but npm's EUSAGE names npm rather than DEP-1 or the registry, and fires in a different job from every other check, which is a third-outcome result and not a pass. Source mapping, package.json overrides, cross-surface digest equality, the window number and publish-date parsing have no predicate (E-37); the image check cannot see Docker Hub shorthand or an extensionless Dockerfile (E-38); the tool is fixture-free (E-28).

Source mapping is deletable unreported, package.json overrides are never read, and publish dates are shape-tested only, never parsed against today (E-37).

TEST-3.title: CI loop
TEST-3.note: Lowered from `proven` to `owed` (the weakest of 2 obligations) on 2026-07-27 by the acceptance test. The loop exists and its five jobs are real; what has never existed is the arming step the whole conditional rests on. TEST-3`s own weakening note predicts this defect verbatim, that the acceptance test must verify instantiation actually arms the gate rather than that the workflow file exists. It ran, and instantiation ships nothing to verify (E-24). Two further measurements from the same run: the `secret-scan` job cannot go green in a seeded project because the manifest`s file set omits `secret-scan.allow.json`, and part C never runs that job, so a red required gate is invisible to the set that exists to catch it (E-25). The roll-up is the weakest obligation, so a built loop that gates nothing reads `owed`, which is the conservative direction the ruling names. Findings: E-24, E-25.

HUM-1.title: Irreversible surfaces get a human turn, unconditionally
HUM-1.mechanism: `.github/CODEOWNERS` covers migrations, contracts and `docs/contracts/`, reconciled against `edition.json``s `irreversibleSurfaces` so renaming one and forgetting the other is loud; docs-lint fails if any of the three loses its owned entry, and fails outside the kernel repo if an entry names only the `@OWNER` placeholder; branch protection requires code-owner review
HUM-1.note: Lowered from `proven` to `owed` (the weakest of 2 obligations) on 2026-07-27 by the first execution of the instantiation acceptance test, which measured both halves rather than reading them. The declaration half was a FALSE GREEN and is now genuinely proven: docs-lint asked only whether an owner-shaped token covered each surface, and `@OWNER` is owner-shaped, so a seeded project with all four placeholders unreplaced passed with every irreversible surface owned by nobody (E-23). Repaired by separating covered from owned, reusing DEP-1`s kernel-context detection in the same file so the placeholder stays legal in the kernel and is refused downstream; red-green proven in a seeded tree with the control that reproduces the hole. The arming half has no artifact at all: instantiation ships one sentence of prose, no script, no ruleset, no readback, and part C`s verification item names no command and leaves no trace (E-24). The roll-up is the weakest obligation, so the row reads `owed` even though its declaration half is now genuinely proven; `proven` beside `mechanism built, not yet armed` was the mismatch all along. Findings: E-23 (repaired), E-24 (recorded, not repaired).

obligations.name: every irreversible surface is enumerated and declared to require a named human review
obligations.text: the three surfaces are declared in `edition.json` and reconciled against `.github/CODEOWNERS`, and an entry naming only the shipped placeholder is now refused outside the kernel repo. Red-green proven in a seeded tree: placeholder gives three failures, one per surface, each naming the path and the claim; a real handle gives ok; the kernel itself stays green because its placeholders are legal there; and the pre-repair predicate with the placeholder still in place goes green again, which reproduces the hole (E-23).

obligations.name: the merge gate requires that review, armed at instantiation
obligations.text: measured absent 2026-07-27: the repository contains no forge API call, no ruleset, no token and no readback, and every hit for branch protection is prose. The acceptance test can verify only what instantiation ships, and instantiation ships an imperative sentence a human executes by hand in a web interface (E-24). Trigger: a ruleset writer plus an armed-state readback, which is also a decision about which forge the kernel presumes.
